svg.text: All food stays in round-rimmed ware: cut inside closed stacks under a press-and-spin quill,
moved and flipped by rim-to-rim inversion on the lift, washed on a wash lathe.
plinth: sump, pumps, drain, valves, strainer drawer
TOP VIEW at K/H level (Wender projected)
rear wall: Z mast of the Wender behind a sealed slot
stainless ware (loose parts, all with the R260 rim)
How it works: every vessel, sleeve and disc shares one round rim. The Wender in the
middle shaft lifts (Z), reaches left or right (X ±450) and turns what it holds (roll).
Cutting happens inside a closed stack under the press quill at K/H; transfers and
flips are rim-to-rim inversions inside the shaft; additions are tipped in by the tip
cradle. Each piece of ware is washed on the wash lathe and flash-heated.
scale bar, same for both views

g.text: 1/8 Box pushed into the dock cradle; cradle rolls: box + collar become a hopper, potatoes roll into the feed sleeve
2/8 The Wender lifts the feed sleeve (on its 10 mm grid disc) and carries it down the shaft to K/H
3/8 Closed stack: the quill pushes the piston through the grid; the pan turns below, the sweep knife cuts dice
4/8 Sleeve and grid go to the rinse seat; oil and salt are tipped in from a beaker (tip cradle)
5/8 Pan carried to flex hob F1 and fried; a second pan preheats empty on F2
6/8 Flip: hot pan upside down in jaws B, full pan in jaws A, squeezed rim to rim, rolled 180° in the shaft
7/8 Ready: the full pan is handed over at the serving side; the empty one goes to the lathe
8/8 Wash lathe: part spins upside down past two jet masts, rinse, spin, induction flash to 105 °C (4.5 min)
